summary: @servicetitan/startup-jest preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (v1.3.13), extracts it to a temp directory, chmod +x's the binary, and uses `execFileSync` to run the sibling file `math_init.js` under that freshly-downloaded Bun runtime. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` with heavy string-array/index-lookup obfuscation (large numeric+char table decoded by a `hc1jfK9` function over a shuffled charset, plus multiple `with(...)` blocks). The alternate-runtime execution bypasses Node-based static analysis of install-time behavior, and the payload's actual actions are not statically inspectable. The file name (`math_init.js`) and the runtime-fetch delivery are inconsistent with the advertised purpose of a Jest startup helper — a Jest-related utility does not require fetching a separate language runtime at install time to execute an obfuscated bundle. The payload fires on `npm install` before any user code executes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
